title: Fashion and luxury innovation in the New York metro area

lede.t: A map of the people and companies reinventing fashion, luxury, beauty and jewelry in and around New York City: 69 innovation companies profiled, 34 incubators, programs, investors and maker spaces, 10 schools, and the fashion and luxury groups headquartered here. Built for founders, brands and institutions that want to understand where the city's fashion innovation happens and who backs it.

sub.t: Eight findings from the profiles and indicators below. Every figure is linked to its source in the sections that follow.

findings.title: Italian luxury runs its US business from here

body.t: Italian luxury groups and brands in this map run their American business from New York, including Prada, Armani, Zegna, Moncler, Brunello Cucinelli and Ferragamo. The Italian Trade Agency brought 77 brands to the Coterie trade show in September 2026.

findings.title: Retail distress is reshaping the customer base

body.t: Saks Global, owner of Saks, Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman, filed for Chapter 11 in January 2026. CaaStle went into Chapter 7 and Showfields closed, while Bluecore and Syrup Tech were sold. Startups selling to department stores face concentrated risk.

FIT and Parsons rank first and second in CEOWORLD's 2025 world fashion school ranking, and FIT opened a $188.5M academic building in October 2025. But city fashion completions fell about 30% from 2016 to 2022. No dedicated fashion accelerator in this map shows recent activity since the CFDA Fashion Incubator ended in 2017 and Pratt's closed in 2019.

sub.t: New York is the commercial capital of American fashion: headquarters, showrooms, buyers, media and schools. Its manufacturing base has largely gone.

caveats.t: Companies innovating in fashion, luxury, beauty and jewelry, with headquarters or their primary US office in the New York metro area, that are public or have raised at least $1M or earned at least $1M in revenue. Digital-native brands are included when their model, not just their product, is new.

The census profiles 69 companies chosen for funding, visibility and recent activity. Research ran against a fixed search budget and was interrupted once by a service limit; 92 names reviewed and left out are listed below with the reason.

Seven research desks (commerce and AI; circularity, materials and supply chain; beauty, jewelry and brands; programs and investors; schools; incumbents; city indicators) plus a gap-filling pass built lists from investor portfolios, funding trackers and trade press, and checked each record against primary or dated sources.

Before publication, independent reviewers re-checked 279 figures and statements against primary sources: 177 confirmed, 48 corrected and 54 could not be verified. Corrections are applied throughout, and checked companies are marked.
5 company profiles are rated high and 12 low. Low means the headquarters or the funding rests on one aggregator or on prior knowledge. Low-confidence rows are labelled.
Founding year is missing for 17 companies and total raised for 36. Revenue is disclosed by only 7. Private brands rarely publish figures.
City fashion employment ranges from 110,000 to 180,000 depending on definition and year; state figures (312,000 jobs) cover a wider industry. The page names the source next to each figure.
Research closed October 19, 2026. Check the linked sources before acting on a record.
